text:
Anna K: Heads-up — saw a reproducible 1.8-2.4x P99 latency regression on TP4 FP8 runs when KV cache is warm and sequences > 1024. Looks like nvlink-bound all-reduce tail.

Sam R: Ugh. Which test? nightly or canary?

Anna K: canary run: `tp4-fp8-kv-warm-2026-03-17` — failure shows during token 2..6 steady-state.

Dave L: Any profiling traces? nvlink bw or NCCL stall events?

Anna K: Pasted perf extract below (shortened):
```
TIMESTAMP  ACTIVITY          GPU0  GPU1  GPU2  GPU3
00:01     allreduce_wait    45%   48%   46%   47%
00:02     compute            52%   50%   51%   50%
00:03     nccl_barrier       40%   42%   41%   40%
KV_CACHE: hit-rate=0.92  avg_kv_bytes=1.2MB
seq_len_dist: 80% 2048, 20% 4096
```

Maria S: hit-rate that high with long seqs => larger per-request kv payload. Batching heuristics may be coalescing heterogeneous seq lengths and causing uneven comm+compute overlap.

Sam R: Could be kernel selection too — our FP8 matmul kernels fall back to smaller tiles at >2048 which increases compute time and shifts overlap window.

Dave L: Try forcing alternate kernel path: set `INFER_KERNEL_HINT=tile128` (dev-only) to see if compute grows but overlap improves.

Anna K: I ran that locally, slapped config, and got better overlap but overall latency still up 15% vs baseline. So compute increase wasn't the main offender.

infra-bot: snapshot uploaded: https://ci.redwood/snapshots/1987654321

Maria S: We should profile NCCL: use `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` during canary to capture P2P stall reasons. Also gather `nvlink` counters via `nvidia-smi dmon` during run.

Sam R: Also try quantization scale variance — FP8/INT8 mixed precision sometimes causes tiny output drift that increases KV cache miss probability (due to routing keys hashing slightly different). Any evidence of increased misses?

Anna K: KV cache hit-rate stayed ~0.92, but observed a ~0.5% jitter in key signatures for identical prompts when using INT8-weighted attention. Logs:
```
key_sig_before: 0x3a1f4e
key_sig_after: 0x3a1f4f
```

Dave L: That explains a few misses, but 0.5% shouldn't spike P99 by 2x alone. My hypothesis: larger kv payloads + suboptimal all-reduce scheduling cause NVLink queues to pile up on a subset of links => head-of-line stalls.

Sam R: Can we run a forced routing experiment: route traffic so that seq_len=4096 only runs on nodes with crossplane NVSwitch topology and compare.

Anna K: Can run tomorrow on dedicated pool. Also proposing a short-term mitigation: enforce `max_batch_kv_bytes=512KB` to cap coalesced KV size and prefer more batches at lower per-request kv size.

Maria S: Add metric: per-batch KV bytes distribution to console. We currently log only avg; need percentiles. I'll file a small console change.

Sam R: If we reproduce, we should instrument the kernel selector to prefer kernels that minimize all-reduce peaks even if compute slightly higher — add a scoring term weight_comm_peak.

Dave L: Agreed. For longer term, look at NCCL schedule tuning or segmented all-reduce to spread across time slices.

Anna K: I'll run the `max_batch_kv_bytes=512KB` canary and NCCL debug tomorrow morning and post updates.

Sam R: Sweet. Thanks Anna — tag me when snapshot ready. :thumbsup:

Maria S: filing infra task RN-6823 to add KV per-batch percentiles and a quick dashboard tile.

Anna K: Thanks team — will update with logs + `NCCL_DEBUG` capture.
